prompt: Implement a two-step delete confirmation with no dialogs: requestDelete, confirmDelete, and cancelDelete drive one boolean and a counter, and each ends by calling the provided refresh().
explanation: A confirmation is really just a tiny state machine: a boolean says whether a request is waiting, and each method is only allowed to run when the state permits it. Guarding confirmDelete with the pending flag is what stops a stray call from deleting something the user never asked about, which is the whole point of the two-step flow. Because refresh() derives every button's enabled state from the fields, you never have to enable or disable anything by hand.
hints: Each method is an if statement around one or two assignments, followed by refresh().
requestDelete has two conditions to satisfy: nothing already pending, and at least one item left.
confirmDelete must both decrement the count and clear the pending flag -- forgetting the second leaves the panel stuck asking.
